approachQuestion.prompt:
Balanced review streak. Each entry is either A or B. Return the longest contiguous interval containing equally many A and B entries, or 0.

Input: labels=[A,A,B,B,A]. Output: 4.

Constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. Labels are exactly A or B. Input is read-only.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Treat A as +1 and B as -1. Use an array indexed by balances -n..n to retain each balance's earliest boundary, initially balance 0 at boundary 0. Maximize the distance to an earlier equal balance.
options.feedback: Equal boundary balances enclose equal counts. The earliest occurrence yields the longest interval at each endpoint.

options.text: Keep only the most recent boundary for each balance.
options.feedback: For [A,B,A,B], replacing balance 0 at boundary 2 loses the length-4 interval at boundary 4.

options.text: Try every interval and compare its two label counts.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

details: Treat A as +1 and B as -1. Use an array indexed by balances -n..n to retain each balance's earliest boundary, initially balance 0 at boundary 0. Maximize the distance to an earlier equal balance.

The signed balance returns to an earlier value exactly when intervening A and B counts agree. Earliest boundaries maximize distance. Balance zero at boundary zero permits a balanced interval covering the full prefix.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the method in the reveal. Choose its tightest worst-case time and worst-case auxiliary-space pair. Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

options.text: O(n log n) time; O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Initialize a balance-indexed array and scan each label once.
details: Initialize 2n+1 slots and scan n labels. The array occupies O(n) space; the answer is a scalar.
Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

Initializing 2n+1 earliest-position slots and scanning n labels both take O(n) time. Each label performs fixed arithmetic and direct indexed reads/writes, so the phases add to O(n). O(n²) would describe enumerating intervals, while O(n log n) adds ordering/search work not performed by this direct-address method.

The earliest-position array has 2n+1 entries even if few balances appear. This is O(n) auxiliary storage; the running balance, best length, and indices use constant state. The O(1)-space option incorrectly omits the allocated array. Input labels and the scalar returned length are excluded, not the working balance table.
